$comment: Shared vocabulary. Jurisdiction files reference levels, mechanism types and property types by id. See docs/DATA.md.

levels.name: Individual
levels.description: Decisions about one's own life, body, property and time.

levels.name: Economic
levels.description: People earning a living, making a profit, obtaining goods and services, using productive resources, building wealth and sharing risk: by their own decisions and contracts, together as partners, shareholders or cooperative members, or through managers, agents and trustees.

levels.name: Non-profit
levels.description: Members governing their own association, foundation or other non-profit organisation.

levels.name: Home
levels.informal: The people living in the home decide among themselves, informally, without formal institutions.
levels.description: The people living together in one home: a house or a flat.

levels.name: Apartment building section
levels.description: Residents sharing one section (entrance, вход) of an apartment building.

levels.name: Apartment building
levels.description: Owners and residents of one building: roof, facade, elevator, common areas.

levels.name: Neighbourhood
levels.description: A city quarter (квартал): walkways, playgrounds, kindergartens, parking.

levels.name: Municipality
levels.description: The basic unit of local self-government.

levels.name: County
levels.description: Intermediate level: county, district, oblast, province.

levels.name: State / canton
levels.description: Federated state, canton, Land. Not applicable in unitary countries.

levels.name: Union
levels.description: Supranational union, e.g. the European Union.

referendum.name: Referendum
referendum.description: A vote of all residents that decides a question.

general_assembly.name: General assembly
general_assembly.description: A meeting of all residents or owners that takes decisions.

personal_autonomy.name: Personal autonomy
personal_autonomy.longName: Personal autonomy over one's own affairs
personal_autonomy.description: The person decides alone, protected from interference.

household.name: Household decision
household.description: The people living in a home decide about it together, protected from outside interference.

council.name: Council
council.description: The council of this community, which decides its affairs.

executive.name: Executive
executive.description: The mayor, manager or head of this community.

upper_council_seat.name: Representative in the higher council
upper_council_seat.description: No body of its own, but does the community at least elect its own accountable member of the council above?
upper_council_seat.$comment: Fallback mechanism: weighted at 40%, and void unless the higher council is elected in local districts, so this community has its own representative.

agent.name: Agents
agent.description: People authorised to decide or sign on someone else's behalf: holders of a power of attorney, commercial agents, brokers, procurators.

trustee.name: Trustees
trustee.description: People who hold and manage property for others (the beneficiaries): trustees of a trust, portfolio and fund managers.

exists.name: Exists in law
exists.description: The law should provide this mechanism at this level.

binding.name: Legally binding
binding.description: The outcome should bind the authorities, not be merely advisory.

no_quorum.name: No participation quorum requirement
no_quorum.description: The result should count regardless of turnout, so that abstainers cannot defeat it by staying home.

explainer.title: Effects of a participation quorum
quote: Participation quorum - the additional requirement that a certain minimum number of votes must be cast in order for a referendum to be legally valid - means that it is in the interests of a proposal’s opponents to abstain rather than to vote against it, so that the quorum is not met. The opponents need only desert the ballot box in order to impose their viewpoint, even when they are very much in the minority. All others who are not voting for other reasons, including those with no opinion, are effectively also voting against the referendum.

The participation quorum requirement encourages a host of controversial election practices such as falsifying the turn-out rate, voter suppression and manipulating the date of the referendum to reduce turnout. It has been shown both empirically and mathematically that a participation quorum requirement reduces turnout to below the quorum threshold, which is known as the "quorum paradox" (a form of the no-show paradox).

The "quorum paradox" arises from the fact that, unlike in deliberative bodies such as parliaments—where a vote can be postponed to a later meeting if a quorum is not reached—referendums cannot be rescheduled.

An example of the participation quorum phenomenon is the 2005 Italian fertility laws referendum, in which the opposition to the proposed loosening of laws on research on embryos and on allowing in-vitro fertilization, campaigned for people to abstain from voting to drive down turnout. Although a majority of people voted yes for the changes in the law, the results were invalid because participation was low.
The European Commission for Democracy through Law (Venice Commission) recommends against any quorum requirements in its Code for Good Practice on Referendums.

concrete_proposals.name: Concrete proposals available
concrete_proposals.description: People should decide on specific, worded proposals, not only on vague questions.

citizen_triggered.name: Citizens can trigger it
citizen_triggered.description: Residents should be able to start it themselves, without permission from officials.

reasonable_signatures.name: Reasonable petition requirements
reasonable_signatures.description: Signature thresholds and deadlines should be achievable for ordinary residents.

broad_scope.name: Covers the interests
broad_scope.longName: It covers the shared interests of the level
broad_scope.description: It should cover the level's shared interests, with few excluded topics; budget and local fees should be decidable too.

no_outside_override.name: No outside interference
no_outside_override.description: People who do not share the interests should not be able to interfere in the decision: to forbid it, require permission for it, veto it or overturn it (as a censor does between author and publisher).

own_means.name: Means to implement
own_means.longName: The community has its own means to implement decisions
own_means.description: The community should control a budget or resources to carry out its decisions.
own_means.$comment: Used for direct mechanisms (general meetings). For representative bodies it is part of Powers (binding_powers).

binding_powers.name: Powers
binding_powers.longName: The body has the powers to govern the community's interests
binding_powers.description: It should be able to take binding decisions on the community's shared interests and have the means to carry them out: its own budget, taxes and fees, and control of local services.

individual_vote.name: Individual accountability
individual_vote.description: Voters should choose between individual candidates (single-member districts or fully open lists), not only party lists, so that each representative is personally accountable to them.

recall.name: Recall possible
recall.description: Voters should be able to remove the representative before the end of term.

no_topic_restrictions.name: No topic restrictions
no_topic_restrictions.longName: No topics are excluded from the referendum
no_topic_restrictions.description: Any matter within the competence of the level should be open to a vote, including the budget and taxes.

local_districts.name: Elected in local districts
local_districts.longName: Members are elected in districts within the community
local_districts.description: Each part of the community should elect its own representative, who answers to it, instead of one list for the whole area.

no_roadblocks.name: No roadblocks
no_roadblocks.longName: No other roadblocks in the procedure
no_roadblocks.description: There should be no smaller procedural obstacles that can stop or stall the mechanism, such as a petition lapsing when parliament or the council changes.

home_inviolable.name: Home is inviolable
home_inviolable.longName: No one may enter the home without consent
home_inviolable.description: Outsiders, including the authorities, should not enter or search the home without the occupants' consent or a court's permission, except in emergencies.

family_privacy.name: Privacy
family_privacy.longName: Private and family life are protected
family_privacy.description: There should be no unlawful interference in private and family life or in correspondence.

home_property.name: Property
home_property.longName: The home is the owners' property
home_property.description: Private property, including the home, should be inviolable.

parental_rights.name: Parental rights
parental_rights.description: Raising children should be the parents' right and duty; only a court should be able to restrict it, on grounds set by law.

joint_decisions.name: Decided together
joint_decisions.description: The adults of the household should decide its matters together and as equals.

child_rights.name: Child rights
child_rights.longName: Children are protected, also from their own family
child_rights.description: The household is only as free as its members: a child's own rights should be protected, with outside help as a last resort.

abuse_protection.name: Domestic abuse protection
abuse_protection.longName: Members are protected from domestic abuse
abuse_protection.description: Victims should be able to get protection, including removing the abuser from the home.

education_choice.name: Education choice
education_choice.longName: Parents choose how their children are educated
education_choice.description: Parents should be able to choose the form of education, including at home, without needing an authority's approval.

chosen_by_represented.name: Chosen by the represented
chosen_by_represented.description: The people whose interests are represented should choose the agent or trustee themselves.

revocable.name: Revocable
revocable.longName: The people represented can remove them
revocable.description: The people represented should be able to withdraw the authority or replace the agent or trustee.

must_account.name: Must account
must_account.longName: They must report and show the books
must_account.description: The agent or trustee should report to the people represented and account for what they did with their affairs and property.

duty_of_loyalty.name: Duty of loyalty
duty_of_loyalty.longName: They may not act for their own benefit against the represented
duty_of_loyalty.description: The agent or trustee should act in the interest of the people represented, avoid conflicts of interest and not profit at their expense.

citizen_initiative.name: Citizen initiative
citizen_initiative.description: Citizens collect signatures to put their own proposal to a vote of all.

veto_referendum.name: Veto referendum
veto_referendum.description: Citizens collect signatures to put a decision already adopted by the council or parliament to a vote, which can overturn it.

mandatory_referendum.name: Mandatory referendum
mandatory_referendum.description: Certain decisions, such as constitutional changes, automatically go to a vote of all.
